title: Microbatch sequence summarizer and pad evaporator
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In bursts with heterogeneous sequence lengths we waste GPU cycles due to padding during prefill and decode. Existing bucketizers favor coarse bins which either overpad or increase fragmentation that harms kernel selection and KV cache locality. Goal: implement a lightweight summarizer that produces representative microbatch length signals and a pad evaporation pass that opportunistically shrinks padded slots during prefill/decode without violating SLOs. The feature should: 1) reduce mean pad tokens per-request by >= 30% for mixed workloads, 2) avoid >5% p99 decode latency regression, 3) be kernel-aware so we can prefer attention kernels (dense/sparse/sliced) based on the merged microbatch shape. Scope: runtime-only changes (serving layer + scheduler), small SDK opt-in flag, integration tests, and benchmark dashboards. Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, heavy changes to client routing. Design sketch: - Summarizer: per-inflight microbatch maintain lightweight token-length histogram and prefix-hash fingerprint; compute a representative length metric (trimmed mean + high-percentile guard). Use a short-lived reservoir (N=128) to avoid cross-request leakage. - Pad evaporator: after prefill packing, run a pass that re-evaluates per-slot effective length using summarizer signals and recent KV hits, then compact sequences into fewer slots when safe (keeps order, updates attention masks, rewrites KV metadata). Evaporation prioritized when inferred pad > PAD_THRESH (configurable). - Kernel hints: expose a compact shape descriptor to kernel selector so it can choose optimized attention kernels (sliced-attn, block-sparse, fused matmul) or a fallback dense kernel. - Prefill/Decode scheduler: interleave small decode windows with prefill packing to avoid stalling short-lived streams; adopt a low-latency fast-path for <16-token decodes. Acceptance criteria and observability described below.

decisions: Use trimmed-mean representative length (drop top 5% outliers) instead of median to better reflect heavy-tailed conversational workloads.
Expose a compact shape hint to the kernel selector (8 bytes) rather than full histogram to keep scheduling fast.
Pad evaporation will be opt-in initially and gated behind runtime feature flag 'pad_evap_v1' and a per-customer rollout in Dedicated.
KV metadata rewrites will be amortized into a per-GPU compaction batch to avoid per-request overhead.
Fast-path for short decodes (<16 tokens) implemented in scheduler to reduce tail latency impact of packing decisions.
risks: Incorrect compaction could cause attention mask misalignment; mitigated by strict validation and unit tests that assert KV slot consistency.
Kernel selector hint becomes stale for long-running streams; mitigated by periodic re-evaluation and TTL for shape hints.
Amortized KV rewrites might introduce bursts of work on compaction windows under high load; plan includes adaptive compaction thresholds tied to GPU utilization metrics.
Feature may expose regressions for rare adversarial inputs (extremely long prefixes); added guard to fall back to conservative binning for >90th percentile lengths.
metrics: throughput_target: +12% tokens/sec on mixed trace compared to current bucketizer
cpu_overhead_budget: <2% host CPU increase per inference node
test_plan: Unit tests for summarizer histogram, trimmed-mean computation, and fingerprint TTL
Integration tests: end-to-end prefill->evaporate->decode on recorded traces (conversational, summarization, code completion)
Performance bench: internal-bench mixed-length v3, A/B against current runtime with stable seed; measure pad tokens, tokens/sec, p50/p90/p99 latencies
Chaos tests: simulate node GPU pauses and verify compaction idempotency and KV consistency
Canary rollout: start with 5% of Hosted API traffic (non-enterprise), metrics monitoring dashboard and automated rollback on SLO breach
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmarks show >= 30% mean pad token reduction on mixed-length traces
p99 decode latency regression <= 5% in A/B tests (primary cluster)
No data corruption in KV cache across 100k compaction operations in stress tests
Feature flag and console controls present for per-tenant enable/disable and rollout percentage
Kernel selector correctly chooses optimized kernel for >= 90% of compacted microbatches during bench runs
